w: Shaped like a calabash gourd and built to be the biggest stadium in Africa, this is where Mandela gave his first Johannesburg speech after walking free in 1990, where Chris Hani and Oliver Tambo's funerals filled the stands in 1993, and where he made his last public appearance, at the 2010 World Cup closing ceremony.
s: Mandela's stage - speeches, funerals, a World Cup final
_facts: Also known as FNB Stadium or 'the Calabash', for its resemblance to an African pot/gourd.
Largest stadium in Africa: capacity 94,736 (84,490 during the 2010 World Cup).
Site of Nelson Mandela's first Johannesburg speech after his 1990 release from prison.
Site of the funerals of Chris Hani (1993) and Oliver Tambo (1993).
Hosted the 2010 FIFA World Cup Final; the closing ceremony was Mandela's final public appearance.

n: Malapa Fossil Site, Cradle of Humankind
w: A fossil-bearing cave inside the Cradle of Humankind World Heritage Site, about 15 kilometres northeast of the better-known Sterkfontein and Swartkrans caves that put this stretch of limestone hills on the map for early-hominid finds. Same landscape and the same protected status, with a lot less footfall.
s: A quieter fossil cave in the Cradle of Humankind
_facts: Fossil-bearing cave about 15km northeast of Sterkfontein and Swartkrans, ~45km NNW of Johannesburg.
Situated within the Cradle of Humankind World Heritage Site.
